newsitem.title: UK: Smoking turns your hair grey, doctors say.
newsitem.headline: Smoking turns your hair grey, doctors say.

text.p: Smoking not only ruins your lungs, poisons your spouse and gives you wrinkles -- it turns your hair grey, too, British researchers said on Friday.
Smoking was also associated with baldness in men, John Mosley, a surgeon at Leigh Infirmary in Lancashire, found.
Mosley noticed that many of the smokers he treated tended to have grey hair or, in the case of men, to be bald, and teamed up with a statistician colleague to see if smoking was the cause.

They found a significant link between smoking, grey hair and baldness. "The relation between grey hair and smoking...was consistent for all age groups in both sexes," they wrote in a report in the British Medical Journal.

Twelve percent of the smokers still had their own hair or natural colour against 32 percent of the non-smokers. Fifty-four percent of smokers had grey hair compared with 47 percent of non-smokers. Among men, 35 percent of smokers were bald compared with 21 percent of non-smokers.

Mosley admitted the study of 600 patients could not prove that smoking causes grey hair. But he noted other studies that show smokers have more wrinkles and other facial changes associated with ageing.
"Possibly smoking causes severe disease, which in turn causes biological ageing," he wrote.

He said his findings might help prevent teenagers from taking up the habit. "If young people can be persuaded that smoking will lead to premature grey hair, and in men to baldness, this may offer a promising line of approach in health education against smoking."
